stories.title: Goodman Capital Leads $44M Condo Inventory Loan on Long Island City Project
stories.excerpt: New Empire Group has landed $43.7 million of condominium inventory financing for a newly built luxury housing development in Long Island City, Queens, Commercial Observer has learned. Goodman Capital provided a $39.5 million senior loan secured by for the developer’s unsold condos at its 117-unit Radiant project on 24-01 Queens Plaza North that was completed in June. JEMM Capital Partners also supplied a $4.2 million mezzanine loan as part of the transaction that refinances past debt and supports the sponsor through the sale of the remaining residences. “Our financing gives the sponsor the time and flexibility to sell the remaining residences at full value, Etan Slomovic, partner at Goodman Capital, said in a statement. Apex Capital negotiated the financing with a team led by Vincent Martucci and Sana Khaliq. Located steps from the Queensboro Plaza subway station, the 19-story condo building was designed by ODA New York with interiors by Paris Forino. Resident amenities include a fitness center, an indoor basketball court, a billiards room, a sauna, a golf simulator, and a rooftop terrace with a lounge and grilling station. “Radiant is a high-quality, newly delivered building in an excellent location,” Eric Goodman, managing partner at Goodman Capital, said in a statement. New Empire Group did not immediately return a request or comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Goodman Capital $39.5M senior + JEMM $4.2M mezz on 117-unit condo project, Long Island City.
Radiant at 24-01 Queens Plaza completed June 2025; inventory financing enables extended sales window.
Transit-proximate (Queensboro Plaza) luxury condo signals strong Queens demand, financing availability for unsold units.
stories.summary: New Empire Group secured $43.7M in condo inventory financing (senior + mezzanine) from Goodman Capital and JEMM Capital for the Radiant project, a 117-unit luxury condo tower in Long Island City that finished in June 2025. The financing refinances prior debt and provides runway to sell remaining units at full value. Located near Queensboro Plaza subway, the project reflects active capital deployment for condo inventory despite market headwinds.
stories.impact: Condo inventory financing availability and lender comfort with luxury-focused projects near transit in Queens suggests sustained investor confidence in the outer-borough rental pipeline and signals that financing constraints are easing for completed projects. The extended sales window may also indicate softer absorption or pricing pressure in NYC condo market, worth monitoring for rental-conversion opportunities in Long Island City.

stories.title: Prime Finance Provides $57M Refi for East Village Multifamily Complex
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between 109Co and Meadow Partners has secured $56.7 million to refinance a two-building multifamily apartment complex in Manhattan’s East Village, Commercial Observer can first report. Prime Finance provided the debt, while a Walker & Dunlop team of Dustin Stolly, Aaron Appel, Jonathan Schwartz, Keith Kurland, Adam Schwartz, Sean Reimer, Michael Ianno and Emily Robertson arranged the transaction. Located at 305 East 11th Street and 310 East 12th Street, the complex includes 88 units ranging from studios to four-bedroom apartments. The complex includes elevators, an outdoor garden area, personal storage areas, on-site security systems and a new fitness center. The property has recently been renovated by sponsorship, which will see 109Co manage each building through 620 MGMT, a dedicated property management platform. 109Co and Meadow Partners did not respond to requests for comment. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: 109Co and Meadow Partners refinance 88-unit East Village complex for $56.7M via Prime Finance.
Two-building portfolio (305 East 11th, 310 East 12th) recently renovated; 620 MGMT providing dedicated ops.
Refi at scale in prime Manhattan submarket signals strong NOI, stable multifamily fundamentals in East Village.
stories.summary: A joint venture between 109Co and Meadow Partners refinanced an 88-unit, two-building multifamily complex in Manhattan's East Village for $56.7M through Prime Finance, with Walker & Dunlop arranging. The buildings at 305 East 11th and 310 East 12th Streets have undergone recent renovations and will be managed through 620 MGMT. The transaction reflects stable underwriting and lender appetite in the submarket.
stories.impact: Successful refi of recently renovated East Village stock at strong LTV indicates robust fundamentals and renter demand in one of Manhattan's tightest, highest-rent submarkets. This signals low distress risk in prime inventory but also reinforces scarcity and pricing power—key for rental-development underwriting in competitive East Village submarkets where acquisition opportunities remain limited and cap rates compressed.

stories.title: LG Ads Relocates from Coworking Space into First Permanent NYC Headquarters
stories.excerpt: Avison Young arranged a 20,748-square-foot lease on behalf of LG Ads, the advertising division of LG, at 115 Broadway in Lower Manhattan, establishing the global adtech company’s first permanent New York City headquarters. The relocation from coworking space more than doubles the company’s footprint in the market. Senior director Peter Johnson and associate Ryan Grecco of Avison Young represented LG Ads. “LG Ad Solutions’ commitment at 115 Broadway illustrates Downtown’s appeal to technology and advertising companies seeking accessibility, workplace quality and long-term value,” said Johnson. “Our role was to translate those advantages into the right fit for LG’s team, its future hiring plans and broader business objectives.” Avison Young has served as LG Ads’ exclusive real estate advisor since 2021, supporting the company’s growth from approximately 100 employees to more than 600 globally. During that time, LG Ads expanded its footprint across multiple markets. The post LG Ads Relocates from Coworking Space into First Permanent NYC Headquarters appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: LG Ads (LG subsidiary, 600+ employees globally) leased 20,748 sq ft at 115 Broadway, Lower Manhattan.
Relocated from coworking; first permanent NYC HQ, more than doubles footprint in market.
Tech/adtech company expansion signals downtown office recovery and rising renter demand in Lower Manhattan.
stories.summary: LG Ads, the advertising division of LG, signed a 20,748-square-foot lease at 115 Broadway in Lower Manhattan, marking its first permanent NYC headquarters and more than doubling its footprint in the market. The relocation from coworking reflects the company's headcount growth from ~100 to 600+ employees globally over the period Avison Young has advised. The move underscores demand for quality, long-term office space in downtown Manhattan.
stories.impact: A 600-person tech/adtech employer establishing permanent headquarters in Lower Manhattan signals growing white-collar employment and population stabilization in downtown, driving renter demand for apartments in adjacent neighborhoods (Financial District, Tribeca, South Village). This trend, if replicated across tech and financial services, increases urgency to underwrite and acquire rental developments in lower Manhattan submarkets ahead of wage-driven rent escalation.

stories.title: Atla Lands Lands $140M to Build Rental Tower in Fort Lauderdale
stories.excerpt: Alta Developers nabbed a $140.2 million construction loan for a luxury rental skyscraper in Fort Lauderdale, Fla. JVP Management, serving as an administrative agent, assumed a loan with $10.4 million of outstanding debt and increased it by $129.8 million, according to mortgage documents. The development, called Alta New River, will feature 400 apartments and a nine-story parking garage. The 35-story building will rise at 100 Southwest Sixth Street, just east of train tracks for the Brightline, about two blocks south of the New River, near the city’s downtown. Units will average about 840 square feet. Construction started last week and is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter of 2028, with Kaufman Lynn Construction serving as general contractor. The Miami-based developer purchased the 1-acre parcel for $20.8 million in 2022. “Alta New River is the kind of well-located, high-quality project we look to finance,” Anthony Shaskus, head of credit strategies at JVP Management, said in a statement. “Downtown Fort Lauderdale continues to see steady renter demand for new, highly amenitized products.” Over the past year, average rents in the city have held steady, hovering around $2,250 per month, according to Apartments.com. Other multifamily projects in the pipeline include Dependable Equities’ two-tower complex and Grover Corlew’s project next to the Citrix headquarters, for which it secured a $92 million financing construction package. Led by Raimundo Onetto, Alta Developers specializes in residential development across South Florida. Last month, it completed the Casa Bella Residences by B&B Italia luxury condo tower in Miami, in partnership with Related Group, and nabbed a $60 million construction loan for a 308-unit development at the southern end of Miami-Dade County. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Atla Developers secured $140.2M construction loan for 400-unit luxury rental tower in Fort Lauderdale.
Alta New River: 35-story, 840-sq-ft avg units, downtown location, delivery Q4 2028; $20.8M land purchase 2022.
Strong construction financing availability and lender confidence in downtown Fort Lauderdale rental demand.
stories.summary: Alta Developers obtained a $140.2M construction loan from JVP Management for Alta New River, a 400-unit luxury multifamily tower in downtown Fort Lauderdale scheduled for completion in Q4 2028. The 35-story building at 100 Southwest Sixth Street will feature units averaging 840 square feet and a nine-story parking garage. The developer purchased the 1-acre site in 2022 for $20.8M; construction began this week.
stories.impact: Strong construction financing availability and lender appetite for new luxury rental supply in downtown Fort Lauderdale indicates sustained confidence in South Florida rental demand and suggests cap rates and yields support continued new development in the submarket. Monitor Fort Lauderdale rental deliveries over next 3–4 years for absorption trends; high supply pace may compress rents and require submarkets (Wynwood, Las Olas adjacent areas) to shift toward workforce/mixed-income products for better returns.

stories.title: BKM Snags Fully Leased Industrial Park with Freeway Frontage
stories.excerpt: BKM Capital Partners has acquired Goldenwest Circle Business Park in Westminster for $62 million. BKM purchased the 12-building park in an off-market transaction on behalf of BKM Industrial Value Fund III. The fully occupied, 231,000-square-foot park sits on 12.3 acres at Bolsa Avenue and Interstate 405, with direct frontage on one of Southern California’s most heavily traveled freeways. That frontage gives the property a level of visibility few industrial parks can claim, according to BKM. “Freeway frontage like this is rare in Orange County, and it rarely comes up for sale,” said Brett Turner, partner and CIO at BKM. “Acquiring it at a significant discount to replacement cost gives us room to reinvest in a location that already works for its tenants. We have income in place as we improve the buildings and common areas, and time to strengthen tenant relationships well ahead of renewals.” Turner led the transaction on BKM’s behalf alongside Michael Grossner, Senior Director of Acquisitions & Dispositions. Darla Longo at CBRE advised the seller in the transaction. The post BKM Snags Fully Leased Industrial Park with Freeway Frontage appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: BKM Capital Partners acquired Goldenwest Circle Business Park (12 buildings, 231k sq ft) for $62M in Orange County.
Fully leased, rare I-405 freeway frontage; 12.3 acres at Bolsa Avenue; off-market transaction.
Industrial value-add with stable income and reinvestment runway; no direct multifamily impact.
stories.summary: BKM Capital Partners acquired the Goldenwest Circle Business Park in Westminster, Orange County, for $62M on behalf of BKM Industrial Value Fund III. The 12-building, 231,000-square-foot industrial park sits fully leased on 12.3 acres with direct I-405 freeway frontage at Bolsa Avenue. BKM plans reinvestment in buildings and common areas while collecting stable income and building tenant relationships ahead of renewal negotiations.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. Industrial acquisition signals stable capital deployment and cap-rate expansion room in Southern California logistics, but does not materially affect apartment supply, demand, or financing dynamics in regional multifamily markets.

stories.title: Marcus & Millichap Completes Sale of Plaza District Mixed-Use
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap finalized the sale of 17 E. 48th St., a mixed-use office and retail property in Midtown Manhattan’s Plaza District. The asset sold for $13.45 million. “This property was a good deal of fun to market. The retail tenant, Hatsuhana, is New York City’s oldest sushi restaurant and recently celebrated its 50th anniversary at the location” said Eric Michael Anton in Marcus & Millichap’s New York City office. “Both buyer and seller worked in a collaborative manner to accommodate each other’s timing requirements. And of course, our closing lunch was at Hatsuhana.” Anton and Adam Steiner marketed the property on behalf of the seller, R.C.L. Properties, and procured the buyer, Lux and Zed Group from Long Island. The nine-story property spans 21,004 square feet on a 2,500-square-foot lot. It was built in 1915 and has been owned and operated by the same family since the late 1980s. The post Marcus & Millichap Completes Sale of Plaza District Mixed-Use appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Mixed-use office/retail property at 17 E. 48th St (Midtown Manhattan) sold for $13.45M.
Nine-story, 21,004 sq ft, 2,500-sq-ft lot; anchor tenant Hatsuhana (50-year-old sushi restaurant); family-held since late 1980s.
No multifamily element; small-scale office retail transaction in Plaza District.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of 17 E. 48th Street, a 21,004-square-foot mixed-use office and retail building in Midtown Manhattan's Plaza District, for $13.45M. The nine-story property, built in 1915 and family-owned since the late 1980s, is anchored by Hatsuhana, NYC's oldest sushi restaurant. Buyer was Lux and Zed Group from Long Island.
stories.impact: No direct multifamily relevance. Mixed-use office–retail sale is a capital redeployment signal in Midtown but does not indicate rental demand, supply pipeline, or financing trends affecting apartment development.

stories.title: Synergy Hosts Official Opening for Massachusetts’ Largest Office-to-Resi Conversion
stories.excerpt: Synergy held the official opening of Altitude Worcester, the largest office-to-residential conversion in Massachusetts, with a ribbon cutting ceremony with Juana Matias, the Secretary of the Massachusetts Executive Office of Housing and Livable Communities , and the City of Worcester. The event also marked the completion of 22 Elm St., the adjacent affordable homeownership community Synergy co-developed with The Planning Office for Urban Affairs. Residents have moved into both buildings Acquired by Synergy in 2023, Altitude Worcester converted the former Fallon Health headquarters, an 11-story office tower, into 198 apartments. The delivery timeline was notably aggressive. Fallon Health did not vacate until its lease expired in March 2025, giving Synergy 16 months to complete the conversion. “Altitude Worcester set out to prove that large-scale office-to-residential conversion could work in Massachusetts, and to do it with real, lasting affordability,” said David Greaney, Founder and CEO of Synergy. “Today, residents are calling 24 and 22 Elm home, and downtown Worcester has new neighbors supporting its restaurants and businesses every day.” The post Synergy Hosts Official Opening for Massachusetts’ Largest Office-to-Resi Conversion appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Synergy completed 198-unit office-to-resi conversion at Altitude Worcester (Mass. largest); 22 Elm St adjacent affordable homeownership.
Former Fallon Health HQ; 16-month aggressive conversion timeline (lease expiration March 2025 to opening 2026).
Demonstrates office supply surplus, acquisition/conversion feasibility, and mixed-tenure affordability opportunity in secondary market.
stories.summary: Synergy held the official opening of Altitude Worcester, Massachusetts' largest office-to-residential conversion, converting the former Fallon Health 11-story headquarters into 198 apartments. The project was acquired in 2023 and completed in 16 months (lease did not expire until March 2025), with an adjacent 22-unit affordable homeownership community at 22 Elm Street co-developed with The Planning Office for Urban Affairs. Both properties are now occupied.
stories.impact: Successful large-scale office-to-resi conversion in secondary market (Worcester) signals viable playbook for asset recycling in markets with office oversupply and tight rental fundamentals. Tight construction timeline and mixed-affordability positioning indicate development feasibility and potential municipal/state support for workforce housing, making Worcester and similar secondary MA markets attractive for conversion-focused development platforms seeking differentiated supply in competitive rental markets.

stories.title: AI Security Platform Ent Commits to Pembroke’s 100 California
stories.excerpt: Pembroke said Monday that Ent has joined 100 California St., leasing the San Francisco property’s newly completed 10th-floor spec suite. An AI endpoint security company, Ent committed to the 10,952-square-foot space for 80 months. Pembroke acquired 100 California in 2014 and has continued investing in the property as the way people use and experience the workplace has evolved. “Creating a great workplace today is about much more than the individual office,” said Stacey Spurr, senior regional director, West Coast at Pembroke. “We take a long-term approach to our properties and continually look for ways to anticipate what our customers want and need. At 100 Cal, that has meant investing in thoughtful design, amenities, service and experiences throughout the building. The 10th-floor suite is a great example of that approach in action.” The Ent deal brings 100 California to 84% leased. JLL’s Matt Shewey, Ted Davies and Carlyle Parker oversee leasing. The post AI Security Platform Ent Commits to Pembroke’s 100 California appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Ent (AI endpoint security company) leased 10,952 sq ft at 100 California St, San Francisco (10th-floor spec suite).
80-month lease commitment; brings building to 84% leased; property acquired by Pembroke in 2014.
Tech tenant leasing signals modest office stabilization in prime San Francisco locations but no apartment demand signal.
stories.summary: Pembroke announced that Ent, an AI endpoint security company, committed to 10,952 square feet on the newly completed 10th-floor spec suite at 100 California Street in San Francisco for 80 months. The lease brings the property to 84% occupancy. Pembroke has owned the asset since 2014 and continues to invest in modernization and amenities to attract and retain tenants.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance. Tech tenant leasing at prime address in Financial District suggests modest office market stabilization, which *could* indirectly support renter demand in nearby residential corridors (SoMa, Mission, NOPA), but lacks scale or employment growth signal to materially affect apartment demand or development economics in San Francisco at present.

stories.title: Northwind Provides $231M Construction Loan to Convert 675 Third Avenue
stories.excerpt: David Werner Real Estate and Nathan Berman’s MetroLoft have secured $231 million in construction financing to convert an office at 675 Third Avenue into a 450-unit residential multifamily in Midtown Manhattan, Commercial Observer can first report. Ran Eliasaf’s Northwind Group provided the construction debt, which will refinance existing acquisition debt on the asset and fund a build-out that has already begun. No broker was listed on the transaction. Northwind had previously provided a $90 million acquisition loan to sponsorship, which purchased the property from the Durst Organization in April 2025 for $100 million. Eliasaf told Commercial Observer that his firm felt “very comfortable” with the building’s layout and the experienced sponsorship group, which is led by Berman, one of the pre-eminent experts of office-to-residential conversions in New York City. “It’s a fairly simple conversion, with no structural work,” said Eliasaf. “It’s basically an interior fit-out, and it’s technically [an asset] that spans the full block of Third Avenue from 42nd Street to 43rd Street near Grand Central Terminal.” Eliasaf added that sponsorship had already started construction financed by equity, and that his firm “came in with capital to take it to the next level.” A full 25 percent of the rental units in the property will be designated as affordable housing under the 467-m program, according to Northwind. The construction loan from Northwind comes only a few months after MetroLoft and David Werner Real Estate oversaw an alarming structural collapse in early July at the former Pfizer headquarters at 235 East 42nd Street and 219 East 42nd Street, which is being converted into a 1,600-unit apartment building, with 11 floors being added to the existing structure. Collapsing columns and falling bricks inside the property on July 7 led to evacuations in neighboring buildings and street closures. Workers managed to stabilize the shifting building by the following morning. Eliasaf to
bullets: Northwind Group provided $231M construction financing for 675 Third Avenue office-to-resi conversion, Midtown Manhattan, 450 units.
MetroLoft (Nathan Berman) and David Werner RE sponsors; acquisition loan $90M (April 2025 purchase $100M from Durst).
Conversion simplicity (interior fit-out, no structural work) and sponsor expertise drive large construction commitment in prime Manhattan.
stories.summary: Northwind Group issued a $231M construction loan to MetroLoft and David Werner Real Estate for a 450-unit office-to-residential conversion at 675 Third Avenue in Midtown Manhattan. The financing refinances a prior $90M acquisition loan on the property, which was purchased from the Durst Organization in April 2025 for $100M. Construction is underway; the conversion requires minimal structural work—primarily interior fit-out.
stories.impact: Large construction financing commitment for office-to-resi conversion in prime Midtown signals lender confidence in NYC apartment fundamentals and conversion viability at scale. The $231M deployment to bring 450 units online in core Manhattan will add meaningful supply to Midtown rental market and likely pressure rents; developers should monitor absorption and lease-up velocity to validate demand assumptions. Successful execution by MetroLoft (established conversion player) may attract capital to other Manhattan office-conversion opportunities, accelerating supply pipeline and shifting market from scarcity to slight oversupply in select corridors.

stories.title: BridgeCity Lends $28M for Williamsburg Multifamily Development
stories.excerpt: Domes Properties has secured $28 million of acquisition and construction financing to develop a multifamily project in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, Commercial Observer has learned. BridgeCity Capital provided the loan for Domes’ planned 45-unit apartment building at 87 Havemeyer Street. Domes Properties, through the entity 87 Havemeyer Street LLC, acquired the three-parcel development site for $13 million from Michael Pescatore, PincusCo. previously reported. EJ Ehrlich, director of originations at BridgeCity Capital, said the loan marks the start of a new lending relationship with Domes, which he described as “an accomplished sponsor recognized for their development expertise and exceptional track record of execution.” Domes Properties is a division of Brooklyn-based Domes Management. Meridian Capital Group negotiated the transaction. The Michael Krariem-designed project will rise seven stories and 47,000 gross square feet. Resident amenities will include a fitness center, coworking space, a rooftop lounge, and an outdoor terrace. Domes Properties did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: BridgeCity Capital provided $28M acquisition + construction financing to Domes Properties for 45-unit project, Williamsburg, Brooklyn.
87 Havemeyer Street: 7-story, 47k sq ft, $13M land purchase; amenities include fitness, coworking, rooftop lounge.
New lending relationship; Domes recognized for execution; marks smaller-scale, neighborhood-focused development in tight Williamsburg market.
stories.summary: Domes Properties secured $28M in acquisition and construction financing from BridgeCity Capital for a planned 45-unit multifamily project at 87 Havemeyer Street in Williamsburg, Brooklyn. The developer purchased the three-parcel site for $13M and will build a seven-story, 47,000-gross-square-foot building with fitness center, coworking space, rooftop lounge, and outdoor terrace. The deal marks the start of a new lending relationship with BridgeCity Capital.
stories.impact: Smaller-scale, neighborhood-focused multifamily financing in Williamsburg confirms lender appetite for new supply in Brooklyn's tightest submarkets. At 45 units, the project size reflects constrained development capacity and zoning in Williamsburg; expect continued supply scarcity and rent pressure in the submarket, making smaller infill developments (5–8 stories, 40–60 units) economically viable. Monitor Williamsburg deliveries and rent absorption—if ongoing, this may justify expansion of development platforms into adjacent neighborhoods (Greenpoint, East Williamsburg) with less-saturated land bases.
